The main takeaway from our work is that

the early modern environmental movement was a complex and multi-faceted phenomenon, not a simple, unidirectional process of exploitation and destruction, and not a simple, one-dimensional process of conservation.

the Puritan imperative of "transformation" was a powerful force in the colonial era, and that the Puritan legacy of environmental concern has been largely ignored by environmentalists and ecologists alike.
